items.topic: What is the goal of 'Effort Test'?
items.context: The spec.json has an empty description, so the intent behind this backlog item is unknown. The title 'Effort Test' could mean several things. Clarifying the core goal is the highest-priority unknown — everything else depends on it.

options.label: Effort estimation validation
options.rationale: Build a system to predict how much effort (time/complexity) backlog items will require, then compare predictions against actuals to calibrate the model over time.

options.label: Backlog processing stress test
options.rationale: Create a test harness that exercises the full backlog pipeline (workshop → plan → execute) with synthetic items to validate reliability and performance under load.

options.label: Story point / sizing tool
options.rationale: Add a feature to the swarm-manager that helps estimate and track story points or t-shirt sizes for backlog items, providing historical data for planning.

options.label: End-to-end workflow test scenario
options.rationale: A lightweight test scenario that exercises the swarm-manager's full lifecycle as a regression test — not about effort estimation but about testing the effort of running through the pipeline.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe your own vision for what 'Effort Test' should accomplish.

items.context: Understanding the intended scale helps determine whether this is a small utility, a new scenario feature, or a significant system addition. This affects architecture, timeline, and resource needs.

options.label: Small utility / CLI command
options.rationale: A focused addition to the swarm-manager CLI — minimal new files, quick to build and test.

options.label: New feature within swarm-manager
options.rationale: A multi-file feature addition to the existing swarm-manager scenario (new API endpoints, UI pages, data model changes).

options.label: Standalone scenario
options.rationale: A separate scenario that integrates with swarm-manager but lives in its own directory with its own API/UI.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the intended scale.

items.context: The item is set to priority 3 (mid-range). Understanding urgency helps determine how much upfront design vs. iterative development is appropriate.

options.label: Exploratory — no timeline pressure
options.rationale: This is an experiment or proof-of-concept. Iterate freely, prioritize learning over polish.

options.label: Near-term — needed within a few weeks
options.rationale: Has a concrete use case that's blocking or slowing other work. Needs a focused implementation.

options.label: Strategic — important but not urgent
options.rationale: Valuable for the long-term vision but can be planned carefully and built incrementally.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe your timeline expectations.

items.topic: What file paths are expected to change?
items.context: The spec.json has no acceptance_allow patterns set. Defining expected change boundaries early helps scope the work and enables post-execution validation.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/**
options.rationale: Changes within the existing swarm-manager scenario — broadest scope for an internal feature.

options.label: Targeted subdirectory paths
options.rationale: Specify exact directories (e.g., scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/effort/**, scenarios/swarm-manager/cli/cmd_effort.go).

options.label: New standalone scenario path
options.rationale: e.g., scenarios/effort-test/** if this will be its own scenario.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Specify your own file path patterns.

items.context: The swarm-manager already has backlog management, workshop rounds, execution pipeline, and a UI. Understanding which existing systems this should integrate with helps plan the architecture.

options.label: Extend the backlog data model
options.rationale: Add effort fields to existing spec.json / backlog types and expose through existing API endpoints.

options.label: Standalone with API integration
options.rationale: Build independently but integrate via the swarm-manager API for data access.

options.label: No integration needed
options.rationale: This is a self-contained tool or test that doesn't need to connect with existing swarm-manager systems.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the integration approach you have in mind.

items.text: The spec.json has an empty description and no tags, acceptance_allow, or acceptance_deny patterns. All plan sections are currently TBD. This workshop round focuses entirely on establishing baseline intent — no implementation details can be planned until the core vision is clarified.

The swarm-manager backlog system already tracks items with priority scores (1-5), status lifecycle (backlog → researching → ready → queued → in_progress → completed), and workshop-based refinement. Any effort estimation feature could potentially build on this existing infrastructure.

plan_updates: Updated plan.md scaffold with additional context in Problem Statement section noting possible interpretations of 'Effort Test'. Added a second risk entry for potential overlap with existing features. All 13 mandatory sections remain TBD pending workshop answers.
